candidates.exact_span:
STEP 3:            SCAN POTENTIAL INSTREAM WASTE CONCENTRATIONS AGAINST WATER QUALITY CRITERIA
                   AND ESTABLISH EFFLUENT LIMITATIONS FOR ALL APPLICABLE PARAMETERS
candidates.computation_change_reason: Frames when effluent limitations must be derived from instream waste concentration scanning; different readings of 'applicable parameters' change which pollutants receive numeric limit evaluation.

candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the receiving stream is not designated for the particular uses.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Determines whether any enforceable numeric limit exists for a parameter based on designated uses; a different use-designation interpretation yields different limit-applicability outcomes.

candidates.exact_span: No limits are established if the potential instream waste concentrations are less than the chronic water quality criteria.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Provides an exemption from establishing effluent limits; different readings of 'potential instream waste concentrations' or which chronic criterion applies change whether a numeric limit is computed at all.

candidates.exact_span: The most applicable stringent criteria are used to establish effluent limitations for a given parameter.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Governs selection among multiple criteria columns in the table when more than one use-based criterion exists; interpretation of 'most applicable' versus 'most stringent' changes the chosen Cs and resulting limit.

candidates.exact_span: Water quality criteria apply at the end-of-pipe for acute aquatic life criteria and discharges to public lakes.
candidates.computation_change_reason: Changes the point of compliance and mixing assumptions for acute aquatic and public-lake discharges; different scope for 'discharges to public lakes' alters which limit formula and criteria location apply.

candidates.exact_span: If background concentration exceeds the water quality criteria, water quality criteria apply. And "Need TMDL" shown to the next column of Avg. Mass
candidates.computation_change_reason: Links background-exceedance to criteria applicability and TMDL need; ambiguous coupling of background rule to the 'Need TMDL' column affects whether limits are treated as water-quality-based or deferred pending TMDL.
Converts daily maximum effluent limits to monthly average limits used for compliance comparison; a different divisor or applicability scope changes the enforceable monthly numeric limit.

candidates.locator: Page 6, Section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS
candidates.exact_span: Daily Max. Conc. = Cs + (Cs - Ca)(F*Qa/Qe)                            Monthly Avg. Conc. = Daily Max. Conc. / 1.5
candidates.computation_change_reason: Core effluent-limit calculation; different inputs or algebraic reading of Cs, Ca, F, Qa, and Qe produce different daily and monthly enforceable concentrations.

candidates.locator: Page 6, Section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS
candidates.exact_span: F   = Fraction of stream allowed for mixing (1.0 is assigned to domestic water supply and human health uses)
candidates.computation_change_reason: Sets the mixing fraction in the limit formula; interpretation of which use categories receive F=1.0 versus a lower fraction changes computed allowable effluent concentrations.

candidates.locator: Page 6, Section body, APPLICABLE WATER QUALITY-BASED LIMITS
candidates.exact_span: Qa = Criteria Low flow (4Q3) or Harmonic Mean flow for Human Health Criteria
candidates.computation_change_reason: Selects the receiving-water flow term in the limit equation; choosing 4Q3 versus harmonic mean for a given criterion type changes Qa and therefore the numeric limit.

candidates.locator: Page 6, Section body, PESTICIDES AND PCBS table header
candidates.computation_change_reason: Method quantitation level bounds detectability of reported measurements; different MQL readings affect whether monitoring evidence is treated as a valid numeric result, a below-detection case, or missing evidence.

candidates.locator: Page 6, Section body, PESTICIDES AND PCBS table header
candidates.computation_change_reason: Defines the acute instream waste concentration term used in STEP 3 scanning; interpretation of Ce source and the 2.13 factor changes whether instream concentrations exceed acute criteria.

candidates.locator: Page 6, Section body, PESTICIDES AND PCBS table
candidates.computation_change_reason: Appears as criterion values for multiple pollutants and columns; reading 1E+100 as no applicable criterion, a de facto no-limit placeholder, or a literal numeric standard changes which criteria enter the 'most stringent' selection.

candidates.locator: Page 6, Section body, PESTICIDES AND PCBS table, Diazinon row
candidates.computation_change_reason: This row lacks an MQL value while other pesticides list one; whether the blank denotes no method requirement, an omitted value, or inherited default affects monitoring-obligation and missing-evidence classification for Diazinon results.

candidates.locator: Page 6, Section body, PESTICIDES AND PCBS table, Need TMDL column
candidates.computation_change_reason: Need TMDL entries interact with the background-exceedance rule; treating N/A as no TMDL needed versus not applicable changes whether water-quality-based limits are established and how unresolved limit cases are classified.
